title: A vendor name in a gate's option about a kb source row does not class the gate push
goal: bl_authority.class_reasons leaves a gate design-class when the words that match the push class name a vendor or product in a kb source row or licence note (such as 'the repository licence from the GitLab API'), not a push, a remote or publishing, while a gate about pushing to GitLab stays push-class; a planted pair of gates proves it.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_authority as a;g={'id':'g1','question':'Which row of the duplicated source id stays in kb/public/_sources.csv?','options':['main row (CC BY-SA 4.0)','instance row (MIT, the repository licence from the GitLab API)']};c,_=a.class_reasons({'touches':['kb/public/**']},g);print(c);sys.exit(0 if c=='design' else 1)

notes: Retrospective of SP-bhzxxhub: the worker's gate g1 on ST-apmeih5l (which duplicate source row stays) was made blocking as class push on 'matched GitLab' in an option's licence note; the orchestrator, acting as operator, answered it. Changing the push class's words guards a rule: a gate before any code.
